entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: J. Uma Devi
Bench: J. Uma Devi
 The Hon'Ble Ms. Justice J. Uma Devi
 Criminal Petition No.634 Of 2020
Order:

-
This petition is filed under section 482 of Cr.P.C., to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.299 of 2019 on the file of the Court of the learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Prakasham District, registered for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 273, 188 IPC and Sections 58, 59 & 63 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 (for short "the Act") against the petitioner/Accused No.1 on various grounds.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Prakasham District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner/A.1 and the learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the State.
When the matter is taken up for hearing, it is brought to the notice of this Court by the learned counsel for the petitioner/A.1 that in batch of Criminal Petitions filed to quash the proceedings registered for the offences under Indian Penal code and FSS Act were allowed by this Court vide order dated 27.08.2018 in Crl.P.No.3731 of 2018 and batch.
The case on hand has also been filed questioning the proceedings in C.C.No.299 of 2019 filed for the offence of Transportation of tobacco products.

Following the order passed in the aforementioned batch of criminal petitions, and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed quashing the proceedings in C.C.No.299 of 2019 on the file of the Court of the learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Prakasham District, registered for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 273, 188 IPC and Sections 58, 59 & 63 of the Act against the petitioner/A.1.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Prakasham District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Consequently, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall also stand disposed of.
J. UMA DEVI, J Date : 04.02.2020 Jks.
THE HON'BLE Ms. JUSTICE J. UMA DEVI CRIMINAL PETITION NO.634 OF 2020.
